question: Does TokenBudgetBatcher read-ahead allow a rollout sibling to reach a later training microbatch after the policy version changes, even when max_staleness is zero?

estimand.primary: Fork sibling IDs delivered to the second collated microbatch, their policy-version lag at collation time, and whether each source checked freshness before or after the simulated version transition.
estimand.independent_unit: One deterministic rollout with two version-0 rows and same rollout_id, followed by fresh sentinels.
estimand.resource_budget: CPU-only deterministic queue/batcher fixture; no pretrained model, optimizer, GPU, paid API, or external spend.
estimand.claim_boundary: Measures the production dynamic batcher's look-ahead and collator inputs only; no forward pass, optimizer, gradient, or task result.

method.fixture: Two version-0 fork rows of two input tokens each, then two fresh sentinels. In the transition arm, current policy version advances from 0 to 1 after the first collated microbatch and before the next microbatch is returned. A fixed-version control uses the same deterministic rows without advancing.

failure_criteria: Any pinned source, patch, or script hash differs.
Fixed-version control does not deliver each fork row exactly once.
The harness cannot identify which fork row enters each collated microbatch.
No distinction can be measured between queue freshness-check time and later collation time.
decision_rule: If either source path places a version-0 fork row in a microbatch collated after the transition to version 1, report a use-time freshness gap for that batching path. Distinguish base read-ahead from candidate group-level admission. If only the candidate does so, reject its stronger freshness claim; if both do, evaluate TokenBudgetBatcher prefetch as the primary defect surface. Do not make optimizer or capability claims.
